title: Rigidity of morphisms of finite locally constant sheaves
statement:
Use the finite-coefficient setting $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ of [def-pur-conventions] and [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $T$ be a separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $k$-scheme and let $L,M$ be finite locally constant sheaves of $\Lambda_T$-modules: they are locally constant in the sense of [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf] and have finite underlying sets at every geometric stalk [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk].

1. The ordinary internal Hom sheaf $\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_T}(L,M)$ of [def-pur-sheaf-hom] is finite locally constant on $T$.
2. If a morphism $\varphi:L\to M$ vanishes at one geometric point of every connected component of $T$, then $\varphi=0$. In particular, if $T$ is connected, two morphisms $L\to M$ which agree at one geometric point agree everywhere.

Here Hom and morphisms are taken in the ordinary category of module sheaves, rather than the derived category; the other coefficient versions in the purity conventions are the separately specified coefficient transports. A connected component means a maximal connected subset of the underlying topological space.

proof.text: First find an etale common trivialisation of the two pro-etale sheaves. The two clauses of [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin] give etale lisse module sheaves $L_0,M_0$ and isomorphisms $\nu_T^*L_0\simeq L$, $\nu_T^*M_0\simeq M$. The ring $\Lambda$ is finite by clause (4) of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], as required there. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values] to each etale sheaf, obtaining etale covers with finite constant module values. Their fibre-product common refinement is a cover by the base-change and composition axioms of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Restrict the constant models to this refinement by [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction]. Thus on a common etale covering $u_i:U_i\to T$ we have $L_0|_{U_i}\simeq\underline{P_i}$ and $M_0|_{U_i}\simeq\underline{Q_i}$, with $P_i,Q_i$ finite as sets. Empty covering members may be discarded.

source.place: Tag 099Y, lemma-compare-locally-constant; finite module values and common covering refinement

proof.text:
These same etale morphisms give a pro-etale covering: the comparison inclusion is covering-preserving by [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies the restrictions of $L,M$ over $U_i$ with $
u_{U_i}^*(\underline{P_i})$, $
u_{U_i}^*(\underline{Q_i})$. For completeness, comparison inverse image preserves constant module sheaves for the following formal reason. By the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], maps from a constant module sheaf $\underline P$ to a module sheaf $F$ correspond to $\Lambda$-linear maps $P	o F(T)$: a map from the constant presheaf is determined by its component at the final object and restrictions. The comparison adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], whose direct image is restriction and hence has $(
u_*F)(T)=F(T)$, gives
$\operatorname{Hom}(
u^*\underline P,F)=\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(P,F(T))=\operatorname{Hom}(\underline P,F)$.
Applying these natural correspondences to the two identity maps constructs arrows in both directions; naturality says their composites correspond to the identity maps, so they are inverse. This isomorphism is the identity on constant sections and natural in $P$. Therefore $L|_{U_i}\simeq\underline{P_i}$ and $M|_{U_i}\simeq\underline{Q_i}$ on the pro-etale site. The site/restriction identification in [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] lets us regard these equally as sheaves on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/U_i$ or on $(U_i)_{\mathrm{proet}}$.

source.place: Tag 099Y, etale-local constant models; formal comparison adjunction and constant-sheaf universal property

proof.text:
Put $H=\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_T}(L,M)$. Its restriction to a localized site is the sheaf Hom of the restrictions: at $V\to U_i$ both are $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda|_V}(L|_V,M|_V)$, with identical restriction maps, by [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and relocalization in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Each finite module $P_i$ is finitely presented over the finite ring $\Lambda$: the free module with basis the finite set $P_i$ surjects onto $P_i$, its underlying set is finite, and its finite kernel is generated by the set of all its elements. Apply [lem-pur-site-constant-module-hom] on $(U_i)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to obtain
$H|_{U_i}\simeq\underline{\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(P_i,Q_i)}$.
The module of linear maps is a subset of the finite set of functions $P_i\to Q_i$, so it is finite. This proves local constancy. To check finite geometric stalks, lift any geometric point of $T$ through this etale cover using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift]. Stalks of a sheaf and its localized restriction at this lifted point agree: in the pointed-neighbourhood colimit of [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk], neighbourhoods equipped with a map to the chosen $U_i$ are cofinal, since any neighbourhood is refined by its fibre product with $U_i$; for two refinements of one neighbourhood, filteredness first gives a common refinement over that neighbourhood and then equalizes the two arrows to the pointed object $(U_i,\bar u_i)$. The constant-stalk isomorphism [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk] therefore identifies the stalk of $H$ with the finite module just displayed. This proves clause (1).

source.place: Tag 093T (1), lemma-locally-constant; Tag 0E8H, lemma-internal-hom-restriction; proetale geometric constant stalks

proof.text:
We now prove clause (2) in the ordinary sheaf category. Under the isomorphisms of step 1 write $\varphi$ as a map $
u_T^*L_0	o
u_T^*M_0$. The unit isomorphisms in [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] and the comparison adjunction [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] give the Hom bijection
$\operatorname{Hom}(
u_T^*L_0,
u_T^*M_0)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(L_0,
u_{T,*}
u_T^*M_0)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(L_0,M_0)$.
Let $\varphi_0$ be the image of $\varphi$ under this bijection. Explicitly $\varphi_0=\eta_{M_0}^{-1}\circ
u_{T,*}(\varphi)\circ\eta_{L_0}$; To verify that this descends the given morphism, write $F=
u_T^*$, $G=
u_{T,*}$ and $\epsilon:FG	o\mathrm{id}$ for the counit of the cited adjunction. Naturality of the counit gives $\varphi\circ\epsilon_{FL_0}=\epsilon_{FM_0}\circ FG(\varphi)$. The triangle identities give $\epsilon_{FL_0}\circ F\eta_{L_0}=\mathrm{id}$ and, since $\eta_{M_0}$ is invertible, $\epsilon_{FM_0}=F(\eta_{M_0}^{-1})$. Substitution yields
$\varphi=F(\eta_{M_0}^{-1})\circ FG(\varphi)\circ F\eta_{L_0}=F(\varphi_0)$.
Thus $
u_T^*\varphi_0=\varphi$ under the chosen constant-origin isomorphisms. Naturality of [lem-cbc-proetale-comparison-stalk] identifies the stalk map of $\varphi_0$ with that of $\varphi$. Thus $\varphi_0$ vanishes at the prescribed geometric point on every connected component.

source.place: Tag 099Y, comparison on locally constant sheaves; comparison unit and geometric stalk compatibility

proof.text: On each common trivialising chart $U_i$ of step 1, apply [lemma-constructible-hom-constant-locally] to the map $\varphi_0|_{U_i}:\underline{P_i}\to\underline{Q_i}$. Its source module is finite, so the hypothesis is satisfied. This gives a further etale covering on which the map is induced by an actual linear map of the two constant values. Compose these coverings with $U_i\to T$ using the covering axioms in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and restrict the constant models using [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction]. Relabel the resulting covering $v_j:V_j\to T$, the finite constant values $P_j,Q_j$, and the linear map $f_j:P_j\to Q_j$. Then $\varphi_0|_{V_j}=\underline{f_j}$. No claim that an arbitrary map of constant sheaves is globally constant was made.

Let $x\in T$ and choose any geometric point $\bar x$ over it. If $x\in v_j(V_j)$, the stronger lifting assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift] lifts this same $\bar x$ to a geometric point of $V_j$ over any chosen point above $x$. By the natural pullback-stalk isomorphism [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar], the stalk map $(\varphi_0)_{\bar x}$ is conjugate to the stalk map of $\underline{f_j}$. Under the canonical isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk], the latter is precisely $f_j$: the germ of the constant section $p$ is carried to the germ of the constant section $f_j(p)$, and these germs exhaust the source stalk. Consequently $(\varphi_0)_{\bar x}=0$ if and only if $f_j=0$, for every chart containing $x$ and every choice of $\bar x$. It follows that
$Z=\bigcup_{f_j=0}v_j(V_j)$ and $W=\bigcup_{f_j\ne0}v_j(V_j)$
are disjoint, cover $T$, and that $Z$ is exactly the locus where the geometric stalk map is zero. Each chart image is open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. Thus $Z$ and its complement $W$ are open, proving the required clopen assertion in the underlying Zariski topology.

source.place: Tags 03PR (geometric-lift-to-cover), 03PT (constant stalk via sheafification), 03Q1 (stalk-pullback); morphisms.tex Tag 03WT (etale-open)

proof.text: For any connected component $C$ of $T$, the intersections $C\cap Z$ and $C\cap W$ are disjoint relatively open subsets covering $C$. The prescribed vanishing point puts a point of $C$ in $Z$. By connectedness [def-weil-connected-scheme], $C\cap W$ is empty. Every point $x$ lies in a connected component: the union of all connected subsets containing $x$ is connected, since any separation of that union would separate a member meeting both sides, while each member contains $x$. This union is maximal by its construction. Hence $Z=T$. For each nonempty chart $V_j$ choose a point in it; step 6 implies $f_j=0$, so $\varphi_0|_{V_j}=0$. On an empty chart this equality follows from the empty-cover sheaf axiom. To obtain the global equality without invoking pro-etale stalk conservativity, take an arbitrary etale object $B\to T$ and a section $s\in L_0(B)$. The images of $\varphi_0(s)$ and zero agree after the covering $\{B\times_TV_j\to B\}$; separatedness in the sheaf axiom of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] gives $\varphi_0(s)=0$. This holds for all $B,s$, so $\varphi_0=0$, and applying $\nu_T^*$ gives $\varphi=0$. On the empty scheme the same sheaf axiom for the empty covering already gives the assertion. For two maps on a connected $T$, apply the proved assertion to their difference; its stalk at the specified point is zero, so their difference is zero.
